home-energy-audit.title: Home energy audits in Ottawa: EnerGuide evaluations, costs and rebates
home-energy-audit.description: Book an EnerGuide home energy audit in Ottawa: 26 licensed organizations, local prices, Ontario rebates and what 56% pre-1991 housing means for your upgrade list.
home-energy-audit.lede: 26 NRCan-licensed service organizations deliver EnerGuide home evaluations in Ottawa. Here's what one costs, what it tends to find in Ottawa houses, and which Ontario rebates it unlocks.

sections.h2: What an evaluation finds in Ottawa homes
sections.html:
Of Ottawa's 287,345 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 16% were built before 1961 and 56% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. The typical Ottawa house dates from 1981–1990, and an evaluation is how you find out what that means for yours: the blower door measures air leakage, the advisor inspects the attic, walls, basement, windows and heating system, and the report ranks upgrades by what they'd save.

Ottawa gets about 4,354 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −24.3°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Ottawa International. That's about 11% more heating demand than the middle of the 70 cities we cover. The more heating a climate needs, the more each fix is worth, which is why the evaluation's ranked list matters more in some cities than others.

In the Ottawa (Ontario) part of the Ottawa–Gatineau region, 69% of households heat mainly with a forced-air furnace, 10% with electric baseboards and about 6% with a boiler and radiators; natural gas is the main heating energy for 59% of households and electricity for 21% (Statistics Canada, 2023). The heating system on the report shapes the recommendations: a forced-air furnace invites a ducted heat pump, electric baseboards a ductless one.

Windfall Ecology Centre, one of the few Ontario providers that publishes prices, charges $500 + HST for the initial evaluation and $250 + HST for the follow-up; Reep Green Solutions lists $540. City-backed programs in Ottawa and London quote $500–$700 as typical.

  • Better Homes Ottawa EnerGuide assessment reduction: For a limited time, loan-program participants can receive a $600 reduction on their approved loan after completing the program, toward the required EnerGuide assessment. Not available to applicants who get the $600 assessment rebate from the Home Renovation Savings Program. Details

Most providers quote the initial (pre-upgrade) and follow-up (post-upgrade) visits separately. Rebate programs that pay on measured improvement need both, so ask for the combined price.

• Initial evaluation, about 2–3 hours. The advisor measures and inspects the house and runs the blower door test.
  • Report and EnerGuide rating. You get the home's energy rating in gigajoules per year and a list of recommended upgrades with estimated savings.
  • Do the work. Most rebate programs only count upgrades done after the initial evaluation.
  • Follow-up evaluation. A second visit measures the improvement, which is what most rebates pay on.

sections.h2: Why air leakage matters in Ottawa
sections.html:
Ottawa gets about 4,354 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −24.3°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Ottawa International. That's about 11% more heating demand than the middle of the 70 cities we cover.

Of Ottawa's 287,345 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 16% were built before 1961 and 56% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Older houses usually test leakier than newer ones, and an EnerGuide report compares your result with homes of the same era, so you can see whether your house is typical or a problem.

• Combustion safety. In the Ottawa (Ontario) part of the Ottawa–Gatineau region, the main heating energy is natural gas for 59% of households. A tighter house changes how fuel-burning appliances vent, so the spillage check should be repeated after serious air sealing. Combustion safety testing in Ottawa
  • Radon. Sealing shifts the pressure balance between the house and the soil. Health Canada's 2012 survey found 6.2% of 64 homes tested in the City of Ottawa Health Unit health region above the guideline. The larger 2024 Cross-Canada survey reports 17.0% (1 in 6) of houses at or above the guideline for Ottawa-Gatineau Metro Area (Ottawa-Gatineau CMA). Test before and after big air-sealing jobs. Radon testing in Ottawa

A blower door test is part of every EnerGuide evaluation rather than a separate purchase. Windfall Ecology Centre, one of the few Ontario providers that publishes prices, charges $500 + HST for the initial evaluation and $250 + HST for the follow-up; Reep Green Solutions lists $540. City-backed programs in Ottawa and London quote $500–$700 as typical.

• A calibrated fan is fitted into an exterior door and pulls air out until the house is at 50 pascals, the standard test pressure.
  • The result is air changes per hour at 50 Pa (ACH50): how many times an hour the whole volume of air would leak out and be replaced at that pressure.
  • While the fan runs, you and the advisor walk the house and feel for leaks at the attic hatch, rim joists, pot lights, trim and plumbing and wiring penetrations.
  • A second test after the work shows what changed, and it is what most rebates pay on.

heat-loss-calculation.title: Heat loss calculation in Ottawa: sizing a heat pump for −24.3°C
heat-loss-calculation.description: A CSA F280 room-by-room heat loss calculation for Ottawa homes, sized to the local −24.3°C design temperature: why it matters for heat pumps, what it costs and who does it.
heat-loss-calculation.lede: The heat loss calculation is how a heat pump or furnace gets sized for your house, and the key input is the design temperature: −24.3°C for Ottawa, from NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Ottawa International.

sections.h2: Why the design temperature matters in Ottawa
sections.html:
−24.3°C is the 19th-coldest design temperature of the 70 cities we cover. The F280 calculation works out how much heat each room loses on that design day, from the house's actual walls, windows, air leakage and ceiling insulation.

At −24.3°C, a cold-climate heat pump sized to the calculation can carry most of the season, and the number shows how much backup heat the coldest days need.

In the Ottawa (Ontario) part of the Ottawa–Gatineau region, 69% of households heat mainly with a forced-air furnace, 10% with electric baseboards and about 6% with a boiler and radiators; natural gas is the main heating energy for 59% of households and electricity for 21% (Statistics Canada, 2023).

Contractors who size by square footage routinely oversize. An oversized heat pump costs more to buy, cycles on and off, dehumidifies poorly in summer and wears faster. An undersized one leans on backup heat. The F280 report is the evidence either way, and it's worth having before you compare quotes.

About $150–$400 as a standalone calculation (a September 2026 planning range; quotes vary). Many energy advisors bundle it with an EnerGuide evaluation, which also gives the calculation measured air-leakage data instead of an assumption.

ventilation-assessment.h1: Ventilation and humidity assessments in Ottawa
ventilation-assessment.title: Ventilation and humidity assessment in Ottawa: condensation, mold and HRVs
ventilation-assessment.description: Why Ottawa homes get window condensation and musty air, what a ventilation and humidity assessment measures, and when an HRV or ERV makes sense. 32% of local houses were built since 2001.
ventilation-assessment.lede: Condensation on windows, musty basements and stuffy bedrooms are ventilation and humidity problems, and they're easy to confuse with insulation problems. A ventilation assessment measures which one you have.

sections.h2: Why Ottawa homes get humidity problems
sections.html:
Ottawa gets about 4,354 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −24.3°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Ottawa International. On Ottawa's coldest days, window glass and poorly insulated corners get cold enough for condensation at humidity levels that feel normal indoors, so winter humidity needs to stay at the lower end of the comfortable range.

Of Ottawa's 287,345 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 16% were built before 1961 and 56% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Newer houses (32% of Ottawa's were built since 2001) are tight and usually have an HRV or ERV that needs balancing and cleaning. Older houses that get air-sealed can lose the accidental ventilation they used to rely on.

• Relative humidity in living areas and the basement.
  • Actual airflow from bath and kitchen fans, and whether they vent outside rather than into the attic.
  • How much fresh air the house gets, and whether an HRV or ERV is balanced.

faq.a: Tighter windows cut accidental air leakage, so humidity builds up. The fix is usually controlled ventilation, not leakier windows.

sections.h2: What inspections find in Ottawa attics
sections.html:
Of Ottawa's 287,345 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 16% were built before 1961 and 56% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Attics in older houses commonly have a fraction of today's recommended insulation, and top-ups done over the years often buried air leaks instead of sealing them first.

Ottawa gets about 4,354 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −24.3°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Ottawa International. That's about 11% more heating demand than the middle of the 70 cities we cover. The colder the climate, the faster added attic insulation pays for itself.

Vermiculite. Loose, pebbly, grey-brown or silver-gold insulation may contain asbestos. Health Canada's advice is not to disturb it; have it sampled before any attic work. Asbestos and vermiculite testing in Ottawa

sections.h2: The right order for the work
sections.html:
• Seal the air leaks first: top plates, pot lights, plumbing stacks, the hatch.
  • Fix ventilation baffles so new insulation doesn't block soffit vents.
  • Then top up the insulation. Burying unsealed leaks under new insulation wastes much of the benefit.

What an attic inspection checks.

radon-testing.title: Radon testing in Ottawa: local levels, test kits and certified professionals
radon-testing.description: Radon in Ottawa: Health Canada survey results for the City of Ottawa Health Unit region (6.2% above the guideline), how to test for 3+ months, where to get kits and C-NRPP professionals locally.
radon-testing.lede: Radon is invisible, has no smell, and is the second-leading cause of lung cancer in Canada. In Health Canada's national survey, 6.2% of homes tested in the City of Ottawa Health Unit health region were above the guideline, and the only way to know about your house is to test it.

sections.html:
Health Canada's 2012 survey found 6.2% of 64 homes tested in the City of Ottawa Health Unit health region above the guideline. The larger 2024 Cross-Canada survey reports 17.0% (1 in 6) of houses at or above the guideline for Ottawa-Gatineau Metro Area (Ottawa-Gatineau CMA).

The two surveys aren't directly comparable: the 2024 study pooled about 69,000 volunteer tests and more of them were taken in basements, which partly explains its higher numbers. Neither can tell you about a single house, because neighbouring homes can differ widely.

• Use a long-term test of at least three months, with most of it in the heating season, which gives the most conservative result.
  • Place the detector in the lowest level you spend four or more hours a day in, away from drafts, and follow the kit's instructions.
  • If the result is above 200 Bq/m³, Health Canada recommends fixing it within a year, sooner if it's much higher.

Our full radon testing guide.

• There's no provincial free-kit program, but many Ontario public libraries lend digital radon monitors free with a library card, among them Hamilton, Vaughan, Guelph, Kingston Frontenac, Greater Sudbury, Thunder Bay, Brantford and Waterloo.
  • For a professional measurement or mitigation, search the C-NRPP directory by your Ottawa postal code; it lists certified measurement and mitigation professionals.

• Since January 1, 2025, the Ontario Building Code requires new houses to include a soil-gas barrier and a radon rough-in.
  • Tarion's new-home warranty covers radon remediation for seven years from possession, and the Canadian Lung Association's Lungs Matter program offers up to $1,500 toward mitigation for households with low to moderate incomes or a lung cancer diagnosis.
  • If your level is high, mitigation (usually a sub-slab depressurization fan system installed by a C-NRPP-certified professional) typically costs $2,000–$4,000.

faq.q: Is radon a problem in Ottawa?
faq.a: Health Canada's 2012 survey found 6.2% of 64 homes tested in the City of Ottawa Health Unit health region above the guideline. The larger 2024 Cross-Canada survey reports 17.0% (1 in 6) of houses at or above the guideline for Ottawa-Gatineau Metro Area (Ottawa-Gatineau CMA). Any home can have high radon, so Health Canada recommends testing every home.

faq.q: How long should a radon test take?
faq.a: At least three months, with most of it during the heating season. Short tests can't tell you your long-term average.

faq.q: Where can I get a radon test kit in Ottawa?
faq.a: There's no provincial free-kit program, but many Ontario public libraries lend digital radon monitors free with a library card, among them Hamilton, Vaughan, Guelph, Kingston Frontenac, Greater Sudbury, Thunder Bay, Brantford and Waterloo. Hardware stores and lung associations also sell long-term kits for about $30–$60.

faq.q: What does radon mitigation cost?
faq.a: Typically $2,000–$4,000 for a sub-slab depressurization system installed by a C-NRPP-certified professional.

mold-testing.h1: Mold and air quality testing in Ottawa
mold-testing.title: Mold testing in Ottawa: air quality sampling and finding the moisture source
mold-testing.description: Mold and indoor air quality testing in Ottawa: when sampling is worth $300–$600, why cold winters cause condensation, and how to find an accredited lab.
mold-testing.lede: Mold sampling tells you whether there's a hidden mold problem and roughly where. It doesn't tell you why, and fixing the moisture source is the actual cure.

sections.h2: Why mold shows up in Ottawa homes
sections.html:
Ottawa gets about 4,354 heating degree-days a year and has a winter design temperature of −24.3°C, according to NRCan's HOT2000 climate data for Ottawa International. On cold days, exterior corners, closets on outside walls and window frames get cold enough for condensation, which is where mold usually starts in Ottawa houses.

Of Ottawa's 287,345 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 16% were built before 1961 and 56% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census. Older basements without a moisture barrier and houses that were air-sealed without adding ventilation are common trouble spots.

• You smell mustiness but can't find the source.
  • After a leak or flood, to check that cleanup worked.
  • Before buying an older house with signs of past water damage.

If you can see mould, you usually don't need a test to know it's there; you need to fix the moisture and clean it up properly.

No Canadian province has a mandatory mould standard for homes. Health Canada's guideline sets no numerical limit: it says to fix moisture problems and clean up visible mould.

Ask any Ottawa tester which lab analyzes their samples, and look for one accredited under AIHA's EMLAP program for environmental microbiology. Pair sampling with a ventilation and humidity assessment, which finds the cause.

Ventilation and humidity assessments in Ottawa · Our mold and indoor air quality guide

faq.q: How much does mold testing cost in Ottawa?
faq.a: Plan on about $300–$600 for a typical sampling visit (a September 2026 planning range); lab fees for extra samples add to that.

faq.q: Do I need a test if I can see mould?
faq.a: Usually not. Visible mould needs cleanup and a fix for the moisture source. Testing helps most when you suspect mould you can't see.

faq.q: Is there a legal mould limit for homes in Canada?
faq.a: No. Health Canada sets no numerical limit; its guidance is to control moisture and clean up mould. Quebec has a voluntary handling standard.

asbestos-testing.h1: Asbestos and vermiculite testing in Ottawa
asbestos-testing.title: Asbestos testing in Ottawa: vermiculite, labs and the Ontario rules
asbestos-testing.description: Asbestos and vermiculite testing in Ottawa, where 56% of houses were built before 1991: what to sample, lab costs and the Ontario rules for renovation.
asbestos-testing.lede: About 160,300 Ottawa houses (56%) were built before 1991, when asbestos still turned up in insulation, flooring, plaster and duct wrap. A lab test before renovation is the only way to know.

sections.h2: Where asbestos shows up in Ottawa houses
sections.html:
Of Ottawa's 287,345 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 16% were built before 1961 and 56% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census.

  • Vermiculite attic insulation: loose, pebbly, grey-brown or silver-gold granules.
  • Vinyl floor tiles and their adhesive, textured ceilings and some plaster.
  • Duct wrap and pipe insulation on older heating systems.

In Ontario, O. Reg. 278/05 sets the rules for contractors working with asbestos. Owners must have materials checked before arranging renovation or demolition work, but that duty doesn't apply to an owner-occupied house or a building of four units or fewer, so testing your own home is your decision.

Whatever the rules, don't sand, cut or remove suspect material yourself before it's tested.

A trained assessor takes small samples, and an accredited lab analyzes them; plan on about $50–$150 per sample. Asbestos labs in Canada are typically accredited under NIST's NVLAP program.

Our asbestos and vermiculite guide · Attic inspections in Ottawa

faq.q: Do I need an asbestos test before renovating in Ottawa?
faq.a: If the house was built before 1991 and the work will disturb insulation, flooring, plaster or duct wrap, test first. In Ontario, O. Reg. 278/05 sets the rules for contractors working with asbestos. Owners must have materials checked before arranging renovation or demolition work, but that duty doesn't apply to an owner-occupied house or a building of four units or fewer, so testing your own home is your decision.

faq.q: How much does asbestos testing cost?
faq.a: About $50–$150 per lab sample, plus the assessor's visit. Abatement, if needed, is quoted separately.

faq.q: What should I do if I have vermiculite in the attic?
faq.a: Leave it alone, keep the attic closed, and have it sampled before any attic work. Health Canada advises against disturbing it or removing it yourself.

lead-paint-testing.title: Lead paint testing in Ottawa: which homes are at risk and how to test
lead-paint-testing.description: 16% of Ottawa's houses were built before 1961, when lead paint was common. How to test with $15–$40 swabs or a lab, and how to renovate safely.

sections.h2: Which Ottawa homes are at risk
sections.html:
Of Ottawa's 287,345 houses (single-detached, semi-detached, row houses and duplexes), 16% were built before 1961 and 56% before 1991, according to the 2021 Census.

  • Built before 1960: probably has lead-based paint (Health Canada).
  • Built 1960–1990: exterior paint may contain lead, and interior paint may contain smaller amounts.
  • Built after 1990: consumer paints were virtually lead-free by then.

• Swab kits ($15–$40) give a quick screen of the surfaces you plan to disturb.
  • For certainty, send paint chips to a lab accredited under AIHA's ELLAP program, or hire a firm with an X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analyzer.
  • Test before sanding, stripping or replacing old windows and trim.

Our lead paint guide.

Don't dry-sand, use a heat gun or power-wash it. Contain the work area, mist surfaces, clean with a HEPA vacuum, and keep children and pregnant people away until cleanup is done. No province has a lead-paint rule aimed at homeowners, but contractors in B.C. and Yukon must include lead in pre-renovation or demolition hazard inspections.

faq.q: Does my Ottawa house have lead paint?
faq.a: If it was built before 1960, probably; 1960–1990, possibly on the exterior. Test the surfaces you plan to disturb.

faq.q: Are lead test swabs reliable?
faq.a: They are a useful screen. For renovation decisions, confirm with a lab analysis of paint chips or an XRF reading.

faq.a: Swab kits run about $15–$40; lab analysis and XRF testing cost more and are quoted by the firm.

well-water-testing.lede: Ottawa's large rural area depends heavily on private wells: Ottawa Public Health says there are over 50,000 private wells in the Ottawa area. If yours is, here's how testing works in Ontario.

sections.html:
Ottawa's large rural area depends heavily on private wells: Ottawa Public Health says there are over 50,000 private wells in the Ottawa area.

Local program: Ottawa Public Health runs rural drop-off sites for the free provincial bacteria test (e.g., Navan, Greely, Osgoode, Richmond, Metcalfe, Manotick, North Gower, Kinburn, Constance Bay, Dunrobin, Carp) plus bottle pickup at the PHO lab, 2380 St. Laurent Blvd. Details

Free bacteria testing through Public Health Ontario labs: pick up a kit at a PHO lab or your public health unit and drop it back off. Chemistry (nitrate, sodium, metals) goes to a licensed private lab for a fee. Local health units recommend testing at least three times a year: spring, summer and fall.

• Bacteria (total coliforms and E. coli): at least once a year, and after flooding, heavy rain or work on the well.
  • Nitrate, especially near farmland or septic systems.
  • Metals and naturally occurring contaminants such as arsenic, uranium or manganese when a well is new and every few years after, depending on local geology.

Our well water guide.

faq.q: Is well water testing free in Ontario?
faq.a: Free bacteria testing through Public Health Ontario labs: pick up a kit at a PHO lab or your public health unit and drop it back off. Chemistry (nitrate, sodium, metals) goes to a licensed private lab for a fee. Local health units recommend testing at least three times a year: spring, summer and fall.

faq.q: How often should I test my well?
faq.a: For bacteria, at least once a year and after flooding, heavy rain or well work; many health units recommend more often. Test chemistry when the well is new and every few years after.

faq.q: Are private wells common in Ottawa?
faq.a: Ottawa's large rural area depends heavily on private wells: Ottawa Public Health says there are over 50,000 private wells in the Ottawa area.

commercial-energy-audit.title: Commercial energy audits in Ottawa: reporting rules and incentives
commercial-energy-audit.description: Commercial and multi-unit building energy audits in Ottawa: ASHRAE levels, 2 reporting rules that apply, and 6 utility or government incentives for audits and studies.
commercial-energy-audit.lede: Offices, apartment buildings, retail and industrial sites get engineering energy audits rather than EnerGuide evaluations. Here's what applies in Ottawa: 2 mandatory reporting rules and 6 incentive programs we found for audits and studies.

sections.h2: Reporting rules that apply in Ottawa
sections.html:
• Energy Benchmarking and Auditing Program (Better Buildings Ottawa) (voluntary): Voluntary: the City says participation in its program is voluntary and builds on existing (EWRB) reporting. Open to all Ottawa buildings except small residential (under four storeys). Participants share ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager data and get a free Energy Performance Scorecard and Insights Report; the City says it is 'exploring options' to arrange lower-priced thermal scans. No city by-law found. Ontario's EWRB (O. Reg. 506/18) applies to buildings 50,000 sq ft+. Source
  • Energy and Water Reporting and Benchmarking (EWRB) - O. Reg. 506/18 (in force): Buildings 50,000 sq ft (4,645 m2) and larger. Buildings 100,000 sq ft and larger need a certified professional to verify data in the first reporting year and every five years after. Source
  • Broader Public Sector energy reporting - O. Reg. 25/23 (in force): Applies by organization type (public agencies), not floor area. Source

• Commercial Custom Audits & Studies - Energy Assessments and Meters (Enbridge Gas (Ontario)): Pays up to 50% of eligible costs for energy audits, engineering feasibility studies, steam trap surveys/audits, air and water balancing and metering. The cap depends on the address's previous-year gas use: up to $6,000 (100,000 to under 3,000,000 m3), up to $10,000 (3,000,000 to under 10,000,000 m3), up to $20,000 (10,000,000 m3+, institutions only). Institutions max $20,000 per project; other commercial sectors max $10,000 per project. Details
  • Affordable Housing Multi-Residential Program - energy assessment (Enbridge Gas (Ontario)): Up to $8,000 for an energy assessment (up to $40,000 per housing provider) to find natural gas savings in affordable housing buildings. Details
  • Save on Energy Small Business Program (Save on Energy (IESO)): Free on-site assessment by qualified Save on Energy representatives, then free installed upgrades: up to $3,000 for lighting and up to $2,500 for refrigeration and smart thermostats (up to $5,500 total). Details
  • Existing Building Commissioning (EBCx) Program (Save on Energy (IESO)): Funds retro-commissioning. Investigation phase: up to $0.06 per sq ft, max $50,000 per application or 75% of the participant's cost for the commissioning provider. Implementation and persistence phases: $0.03 per kWh of confirmed/persisting savings (each capped at 30% of annual consumption or $50,000, whichever is lower). Details
  • XLerate Program - Project Feasibility Study funding (Save on Energy (IESO)): Project feasibility study (PFS) funding at a 50% cost share; project incentives of $300/MWh up to 75% of eligible costs (max $15 million per project). Details
  • BizEnergySaver Program (local initiative) (Save on Energy (IESO)): Free on-site assessment plus direct installation, with instant discounts applied on the invoice (most VFD upgrades now free). Details

• Level 1, walk-through: a site visit and bill review that benchmarks the building and lists low-cost measures.
  • Level 2, energy survey and analysis: where the energy goes, with savings and cost estimates per measure. Most incentive applications use this level.
  • Level 3, detailed analysis: monitoring and modelling for capital-intensive projects.

Ask which level a quote covers. Audits are done by engineering firms and energy consultants; look for a P.Eng. and credentials such as the Certified Energy Manager (CEM). How commercial energy audits work.

faq.q: Do Ottawa buildings have to report energy use?
faq.a: Yes, above certain sizes: Energy and Water Reporting and Benchmarking (EWRB) - O. Reg. 506/18; Broader Public Sector energy reporting - O. Reg. 25/23.

faq.q: Are there incentives for commercial energy audits in Ottawa?
faq.a: Yes: Commercial Custom Audits & Studies - Energy Assessments and Meters; Affordable Housing Multi-Residential Program - energy assessment; Save on Energy Small Business Program; Existing Building Commissioning (EBCx) Program. Check eligibility and pre-approval rules before you commission the audit.

faq.q: What does a commercial energy audit cost?
faq.a: It depends on the building's size and the ASHRAE level. Get quotes that state the level and the deliverables.
